title: The facts of a timewalk walk
description: What timewalk-export --json writes: one walk's history and notes, for a class to render its own pages from. Format 3. docs/reference.md explains each field.

format.description: The version of this layout. A change that a renderer must know of raises it.

timewalk.description: The version of timewalk that wrote the file.

made.description: The line that marks the file as made by timewalk-export, which writes over only its own files.

observed.description: Whether the do$ commands ran, so that each do$ line has its writes and each file of a move with do$ lines its by and patch.

mode.description: The mode a tutorial starts in; a narrative is always watch.

loose.description: The globs of the files that a tutorial compares by the names of their packages, such as uv.lock. Since 1.4.1.

intro.description: The walk's text before its first stop.

manifest.description: The slides manifest, from the class folder.

history.description: The commit of every step and move of the whole history, by name, for an item that names another part.

errors.description: What timewalk-check says is wrong with this walk.

warnings.description: What timewalk-check warns of in this walk.

text.description: Markdown, as written, every character of it.

track.description: "" for the shell at the step, main for the repository you started from, runs to runs9 for the Runs tabs.

makes.description: A do$ line: the command that makes the move.

writes.description: For a do$ line that ran: the files it adds, changes or removes, in the order of their paths. null for any other command, or when it did not run.

take.description: Added in timewalk 1.4.3, so a file of an older version has none. In a strict walk, for a do$ line that runs uv and writes a pyproject.toml or a uv.lock of the move that loose does not name, and for each later do$ line that writes a file that those lines write: what do mode gives in place of the lines. null for any other command, or when the do$ lines did not run and give no by.

lines.description: At the first line of a take: the places, from 0 among the move's do$ lines, of the lines that the command stands for, this one first. Empty at a later line that joins an earlier take; files, deletes and command are then empty too.

files.description: The files of the move that the lines write and the move keeps, in the order of the move's files: the command takes them from the move's commit.

deletes.description: The files that the lines write and the move deletes, then the old paths of those it renames: the command removes them.

command.description: git restore --source <12 characters of the move's commit> -- <files>, then && rm -f -- <deletes> when there are any, then && uv sync [--directory DIR] --locked --all-groups --all-packages for each uv.lock in files. From the top of the project.

move.description: The step or move the item names, when it is not the move it is in.

show.description: The lines its show: lines quote, in order.

path.description: A patch$ line: the file that the move changes by a patch, its diff from the commit before the move.

diff.description: The whole diff of the file, from its first hunk; "" for a binary file or a change of mode alone.

by.description: Where the file comes from: the index, among the move's do$ lines, of the last one that writes it; "patch" when no do$ line writes it, so a patch$ line should name it; null when the do$ lines did not run.

patch.description: What a person changes by hand, from its first hunk: the whole diff for a patch, and for a file of a do$ line the diff from what the line left to the commit, "" when there is none. null when the do$ lines did not run.

number.description: The number a reader sees: the name without the prefix of the tags and the zeros in front, such as 8b.1 or 5.3 to 5.6.
The number a reader sees: the name without the prefix of the tags and the zeros in front, such as 8b.1 or 5.3 to 5.6.

files.description: For a stop with no moves: the files of its change from its start. Empty for a stop with moves.
